title: Genome-wide CRISPR knockout screens of bacterial cytotoxins in HeLa cells
author: Yang, Zhou, et al.
materials: Blood & Cell Culture DNA Mini Kit
Gold Hi EndoFree Plasmid Maxi Kit
NEB Next® UltraTM DNA Library Prep Kit for Illumina

steps.title: Seed HeLa‑Cas9 cells
steps.instruction: Seed HeLa‑Cas9 cells into four 15 cm dishes at 8 × 10⁶ cells per plate and incubate at 37 °C in 5 % CO₂.

steps.title: Transduce with GeCKO v2 library
steps.instruction: Thaw the GeCKO v2 lentiviral library on ice, add the virus dropwise to the cells at an MOI of 0.3, rock the plates gently 3–4 times for even distribution, and return the plates to the incubator.

steps.title: Replace medium at 12 h
steps.instruction: Twelve hours post‑infection, aspirate the medium and add 20 mL of fresh complete DMEM to each plate.

steps.title: Start puromycin selection
steps.instruction: Twenty‑four hours post‑infection, replace the medium with 20 mL of complete DMEM containing 2.5 µg/mL puromycin to begin selection.

steps.title: Maintain 2.5 µg/mL puromycin
steps.instruction: Keep the cells under 2.5 µg/mL puromycin for 48 h, changing the medium every 24 h.

steps.title: Reduce puromycin concentration
steps.instruction: Replace the medium with 20 mL of complete DMEM containing 1.25 µg/mL puromycin and incubate for an additional 48 h, changing the medium every 24 h; passage cells to new plates if confluency becomes too high.

steps.title: Harvest and backup cells
steps.instruction: Trypsin‑digest all cells, combine them, freeze half at –80 °C as a backup stock, and seed the remaining half into three 15 cm dishes; grow these to ~70 % confluence.

steps.title: Collect starting library sample
steps.instruction: Harvest one of the three plates, label it as the starting library sample (R0), and use the other two plates for the toxin screen.

description: The protocol below describes the CRISPR knockout screen for TcdB4 on HeLa cells using the GeCKO v2 library. However, we have also used this protocol in other human cell lines and with other genome-wide CRISPR libraries. To minimize possible biases, we strongly suggest using one batch of the toxin throughout the screen. Bacterial toxins can be divided into small aliquots and stored at −80°C for one year without overt loss of activity. The toxin should be used immediately after being thawed, and never refreeze and/or reused thawed toxin aliquots. Earlier versions of this protocol were applied for targeted screens with other bacterial cytotoxins (Tao et al., 2016, 2019; Zhou et al., 2021). For complete details on the use and execution of the protocol, please refer to (Luo et al., 2022).
